name: OpenCV.js
category: A9. Adjacent resources mentioned during discovery
role: OpenCV compiled to WASM: feature detection, filtering, tracking, analysis in browser or Node
summary: OpenCV's computer-vision library built for JavaScript through WebAssembly, published as @techstark/opencv-js (the official docs cover the build). Driven from a script or a browser page on image data; outputs are matrices, keypoints, masks and filtered images. It is the only catalogued option for analysis such as tracking, contours, optical flow and face or marker detection.
use_when: Analysing footage or stills in JS: contours, optical flow, feature matching, marker detection
Over Sharp when you need computer vision rather than resize and convert
Deriving masks or motion data from frames to drive an overlay
avoid_when: Plain resize, crop, format conversion: Sharp or libvips are faster and smaller
Cut detection in video files: PySceneDetect does it directly
Heavy or realtime CV on large video: native OpenCV in Python is far faster

assessment.rationale: Maintained community WASM build tracking OpenCV 5; runs in Node and browsers. Adds computer vision no catalogued neighbour covers (Sharp and libvips only transform pixels). Bundle is large and API coverage is a subset.

notes: 2026-10-26: official_url is the OpenCV docs hub; the JS build is a third-party package (TechStark). Subset of OpenCV exposed; check needed functions before relying on them.
